assessment: Large-cover rework and rounded-corner installation failures suggest two separable fit problems, but neither cause is established. Previous design compliance does not establish future fit, wash durability, or the 32-minute target.

openings.claim: Sewing may introduce cumulative edge-length distortion, making longer panels fail despite correct cutting dimensions.
openings.delta: Test whether dimensions change during sewing before changing the common cutting allowance; a sewing-stage correction could preserve existing cloth layouts.
openings.prediction: Failing panels will match intended dimensions after cutting but acquire measurable length or diagonal error after sewing. Stable sewn dimensions would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Before cutting the whole batch, mark and measure a representative large and medium panel before and after each seam. Use retained offcuts for paired seam trials reversing feed direction while holding operator and stitch settings constant. If drift responds, trial registration marks and staged alignment on an early ordered cover. Record total working time and actual cutting waste by area.
assumptions: Feed-related distortion is a hypothesis, not an observation.
Marks can be temporary and harmless to the ordered design.
Any adopted change must pass the stipulated wash test and fit within 350 units and three weeks.

openings.claim: An internal folded allowance or alternate corner-pocket seam path may let the same printed blank accommodate rounded corners without requiring repeated placement adjustment.
openings.delta: Treat corner-pocket geometry as an independently adjustable feature while preserving the ordered table size, visible design, and purchased cloth.
openings.prediction: On matched tabletop dimensions, the revised pocket will improve first placement on rounded corners while remaining stable on square corners; persistent failure would argue against pocket geometry alone.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner profiles from willing customers. Compare existing and temporarily basted pocket paths using an early cover and the same customer table. Advance only a version retaining visible print placement, tool-free removal, five-cycle durability, measured waste at most 8%, and acceptable working time.
assumptions: Existing allowances contain enough fabric for the fold.
Customer access permits an installation comparison.
Prototype success would still require verification of at least 38 first-placement fits and all ordered designs in the 40-cover batch.
